subject.title: Preserve structured ACP backend error kinds instead of mapping all errors to `end_turn`

question: Should ACP backend failures be represented as structured `RequestError`s, mapped into existing ACP stop reasons, or deferred until the ACP protocol adds explicit failure classes?
rationale: The gateway already exposes structured error kinds, but the ACP SDK stop-reason contract does not include timeout, rate_limit, or server_error, so the permanent client-visible representation needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt structured RequestError rejection
options.body: Proceed with the linked PR direction, using JSON-RPC errors for operational failures and `max_tokens` for context-length failures after upgrade/client proof is reviewed.

options.title: Stay within StopReason only
options.body: Map only classes that fit existing ACP stop reasons and document that other backend failures still surface as `end_turn`.

options.title: Defer for ACP protocol support
options.body: Leave current behavior in place until upstream ACP adds explicit structured backend failure semantics.

recommendation.title: Adopt structured RequestError rejection
recommendation.body: Proceed with the linked PR direction, using JSON-RPC errors for operational failures and `max_tokens` for context-length failures after upgrade/client proof is reviewed.

likelyOwner.reason: The current structured gateway error-kind handling and tests appear in their recent ACP commit, making them the strongest routing candidate for the contract decision.
